2. Heard Mr. S.K. Mishra, learned counsel for the petitioners; Mr. S. Rath, learned Addl. Standing Counsel appearing for the State- Opposite Parties; and Mr. S.S. Kanungo, learned counsel appearing for opposite party no.3.

3 . The petitioners have filed this writ petition claiming compensation for the land and building acquired by opposite party no.3 and further seeks direction to the opposite parties for up-gradation of their category from 'C' to 'A' so as to enable them to get employment under the opposite party no.3 in accordance with law.

4. Mr. S.K. Mishra, learned counsel appearing for the petitioners contended that the predecessor of the petitioners and Hadia Sahoo were in possession of the land in question along with building as per the Record of Rights under Annexure-1.
When the land and building were jointly recorded in the aforementioned names, the same were acquired, but compensation has been disbursed only to one of the co-shares, i.e., Hadia Sahoo.
Consequentially, the petitioners are deprived of getting compensation for the land and building acquired by opposite party no.3.

Apart from the same, after acquisition of land and building, the benefit of rehabilitation appointment was also granted to the legal representatives of Hadia Sahoo, whereas the petitioners have been discriminated.

Therefore,
the petitioners have approached this Court by filing the present writ petition.

5. Mr. S.S. Kanungo, learned counsel appearing for opposite party no.3-MCL contended that when the land and building were acquired by the opposite party, the only competent person was there, i.e.,

sentences.text: Therefore, the compensation amount has been disbursed in his favour with a rider that if anybody raised any dispute, in that case the same can be resolved by the appropriate forum.

Therefore, if the petitioners raised dispute with regard to grant of compensation amount for the land and building acquired by the opposite party, then they have to approach the appropriate forum, i.e.,
C.B.A. Tribunal, as envisaged under Section 14 of the Coal Bearing Areas (Acquisition and Development) Act, 1957.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Instead of approaching the appropriate forum, the petitioners should not have approached this Court by filing the present writ petition.
So far as compensation amount is concerned, since the petitioners are categorized under 'C' category, employment to their legal representatives is not available.

But once the appropriate forum holds that the land and building of the petitioners have been acquired and, as such, they are categorized from 'C' to 'A', in that case,
they are entitled to get the benefit of employment.

6. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and after going through the records, this Court finds that the land and building stand recorded in the name of Hadia Sahoo and the predecessors of the petitioners and, as such, the same have been acquired and compensation has already been determined and disbursed to Hadia Sahoo, who is one of the co-sharers.

Therefore, if the petitioners claim that they have share over the land and building, they have to approach the appropriate forum,
i.e., C.B.A. Tribunal, as envisaged under Section 14 of the Coal Bearing Areas (Acquisition and Development) Act, 1957.

entities.text: Coal Bearing Areas (Acquisition and Development) Act, 1957
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Instead of approaching the appropriate forum, the petitioners cannot approach this Court by filing the present writ petition.

So far as up-gradation of category from 'C' to 'A' is concerned, in the event the dispute is resolved by the competent forum holding that the petitioners are entitled to the benefit, as their land and building have been acquired, then they are entitled to get the benefit in accordance with law.

Therefore, it is open to the petitioners to pursue their remedy before the appropriate forum as per the provisions contained under Section 14 of the Coal Bearing Areas (Acquisition and Development) Act, 1957.

sentences.text: Needless to say, if the petitioners have approached the appropriate forum by filing appropriate application within a period of 15 days hence, the appellate authority shall consider the same and pass appropriate order in accordance with law as expeditiously as possible, preferably within a period of four months from the date of filing such application along with certified copy of this order.
7. With the aforesaid observation and direction, the writ petition stands disposed of.
